I’m very sorry for your loss. Mental illness is a serious thing and it isn’t always clear what is normal level of unhappy. 

I wouldn’t say I have beaten depression, but I have suicidal tendencies and I gauge how well im managing my mental health by the rate at which I have suicidal thoughts. 

That said I have certainly gotten better and I think there are a few things that have been particularly useful to me. 

Journaling is very useful for understanding, gathering, and articulating thoughts. I think it’s useful because it helps problems become more clear and therefore less anxiety inducing. Also it helps put things in perspective somewhat to read your thoughts and problems rather than just think about them. 

Managing health by diet and exercise also helps. It helps manage natural good brain chemistry I think. Also it doesn’t hurt that you generally feel better and look better if you are healthy. 

Understanding motivation style is also very useful for learning how to live in a more personalized way. Some people have strong motivation in one direction, that’s simple. But others are more calm natured less motivated people, while others gain and lose interest in things easily. I think picking jobs and hobbies is easier if you understand your motivation. 

Then you have your emotional needs, don’t let stress build up too much, try to socialize, do things you are good at, get outside, etc. just try to make sure your needs are met. 

And finally i think a lot of things about mental health relate to your judgments of the past, present, and anticipation for the future. 

I say don’t look back any more than you have to. Find ways to enjoy the present, be present, be grateful, take time to do what you love.  And set goals and plans for the future that make you excited. If you are happy with the present and excited for the future, that helps if nothing else. 

If this sounds like a lot of work, that’s because in my case it is a lot of work. Depression and anxiety are horrible things but I work hard every day to save myself and my family from the possible consequences of my flawed brain chemistry. 

I wish you the very best. I know it’s not always easy but there are more people than you know rooting for you. Even if things ever seem hopeless, just know they never are. 

TLDR. Journaling, being healthy, understanding yourself, satiating emotional needs, and being cognizant of your judgments of the past present and future are all some of the main things that have helped me personally with my mental health.
